[[proof of space-time]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bravo-Marquez |first1=Felipe |last2=Ugarte |first2=Martin |last3=Reeves |first3=Steve |title=2019 IEEE International Conference on Decentralized |first3=Marko |class=cs.CR }}</ref>

Filecoins are paid to miners (termed "storage providers" - SPs) who provide storage for clients, as opposed to [[Bitcoin]] where miners secure the network and maintain consensus.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Gupta |first1=Pranay |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UBiBDwAAQBAJ |title=Fintech: The New DNA of Financial Services |last2=Tham |first2=T. Mandy |date=2018-12-03 |publisher=Walter de Gruyter GmbH & Co KG |isbn=978-1-5474-0090-4 |page=148 |language=en}}</ref> The payment amount depends on the network schedule, storage sectors quantity and size, adherence to FIL+ and deals made with clients, and participation in the network requires putting tokens in collateral.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bernardineli |first=Danilo |date=2023-04-11 |title=Understanding the Filecoin Consensus Pledge |url=https://blog.block.science/understanding-the-filecoin-consensus-pledge/ |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=BlockScience Blog |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
Filecoin, as a cryptocurrency and file storage network, was defined in a white paper published in July 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://filecoin.io/filecoin-jul-2014.pdf|title=Filecoin: A Cryptocurrency Operated File Storage Network|author=filecoin.io|date=15 July 2014}}</ref>

The project was launched in August 2017, and raised over $200 million within 30 minutes via an [[initial coin offering]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|date=2017-08-21|title=What are initial coin offerings?|newspaper=The Economist|url=https://www.economist.com/the-economist-explains/2017/08/21/what-are-initial-coin-offerings|access-date=2019-10-05|issn=0013-0613|archive-date=2019-09-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190905234757/https://www.economist.com/the-economist-explains/2017/08/21/what-are-initial-coin-offerings|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2020, the project set up the Filecoin Foundation under the leadership of founding officer [[Megan Klimen]] to support the development of the protocol, and the Filecoin Foundation for the Decentralized Web to support other projects contributing to the ecosystem of the [[decentralized web]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Protocol Labs Collaborates with Consensys to Bring Filecoin to Ethereum |url=https://consensys.io/blog/protocol-labs-collaborates-with-consensys-to-bring-filecoin-to-ethereum |access-date=2024-04-20 |website=Consensys |language=en |archive-date=2024-04-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420024718/https://consensys.io/blog/protocol-labs-collaborates-with-consensys-to-bring-filecoin-to-ethereum |url-status=live }}</ref>{{primary source inline|date=October 2024}}

In April 2021, the storage capacity of the network crossed the Baseline Target, which was interpreted as a transition from a "capacity building" stage of the network to one on which scale was achieved.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bernardineli |first=Danilo |date=2021-05-19 |title=Filecoin Network Crosses Baseline Sustainability Target for First Time |url=https://filecoin.io/blog/posts/filecoin-network-crosses-baseline-sustainability-target-for-first-time/ |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=Filecoin |language=en}}</ref> However, the network growth in 2022 was slower than the Baseline Target,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baseline Crossing - full analysis |url=https://hackmd.io/@cryptoecon/BkytBgbIs |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=HackMD |language=en}}</ref> which caused the capacity to become smaller than the target by February 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kalghatgi |first=Vik |date=2023-02-15 |title=Filecoin Network Crosses Baseline from Above |url=https://medium.com/cryptoeconlab/filecoin-network-crosses-baseline-from-above-585b696083af |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=CryptoEconLab |language=en}}</ref>

Their Board of Directors and advisors include [[Brewster Kahle]] (Founder of [[Internet Archive]]), [[Joseph Lubin (entrepreneur)|Joe Lubin]] (Founder of Consensys & Cofounder of Ethereum), and Denelle Dixon (CEO of [[Stellar (payment network)|Stellar]] Development Foundation).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Filecoin Foundation Announces Board of Directors |url=https://www.fil.org/blog/filecoin-foundation-announces-board-of-directors |access-date=2024-11-26 |website=fil.org |language=en}}</ref>

== Philanthropy ==
In April 2021, the Filecoin Foundation donated 50,000 filecoins worth $10,000,000 to the [[Internet Archive]].<ref name="grant-to-IA">{{Cite web |last=Hanamura |first=Wendy |date=2021-04-01 |title=Filecoin Foundation Grants 50,000 FIL to the Internet Archive |url=http://blog.archive.org/2021/04/01/filecoin-foundation-grants-50000-fil-to-the-internet-archive/ |access-date=2022-09-28 |website=Internet Archive Blogs |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-02 |title=Filecoin Foundation donates $10M in FIL tokens to Internet Archive |url=https://cointelegraph.com/news/filecoin-foundation-donates-10m-in-fil-tokens-to-internet-archive |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230709052443/https://cointelegraph.com/news/filecoin-foundation-donates-10m-in-fil-tokens-to-internet-archive |archive-date=9 Jul 2023 |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=Cointelegraph |language=en}}</ref> In addition, Internet Archive's founder [[Brewster Kahle]] and director of partnerships Wendy Hanamura joined the boards of advisors of Filecoin and the Filecoin Foundation for the [[Decentralized web|Decentralized Web]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Masnick |first=Mike |title=Filecoin Foundation Donates $10 Million Worth Of Filecoin To Internet Archive |url=https://www.techdirt.com/articles/20210404/18351646551/filecoin-foundation-donates-10-million-worth-filecoin-to-internet-archive.shtml|access-date=2021-04-15|website=Techdirt |date=8 April 2021 |archive-date=2021-04-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415134238/https://www.techdirt.com/articles/20210404/18351646551/filecoin-foundation-donates-10-million-worth-filecoin-to-internet-archive.shtml |url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2020, content from Internet Archive started to be stored in Filecoin, with the purpose of creating a decentralized prototype of the digital library.<ref name="grant-to-IA" /> By October 2023, one petabyte of data had been uploaded to the Filecoin network.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joyce |first=Jamie |date=2023-10-20 |title=Celebrating 1 Petabyte on the Filecoin Network! {{!}} Internet Archive Blogs |url=https://blog.archive.org/2023/10/20/celebrating-1-petabyte-on-the-filecoin-network/ |access-date=2025-01-14}}</ref>
